window: It stopped raining an hour ago. I ring the bell. The door opens almost before the bell has finished ringing. Mia hugs me: 'You came. You actually came.'
Julian appears with two glasses of wine. 'There they are. Keep your shoes on, we've got nothing left to scratch.'
Julian raises his glass: 'To fresh starts.' I clink mine against it. Mia passes the noodles.
'Australia,' Julian says. 'Can you imagine me surfing?' Mia laughs, a beat late.
Julian checks his watch at the empty fourth place. 'Seven forty. Even for him that's ambitious.'
He clears the setting. 'He's not coming. Classic Leo.' Mia flinches as he does it. 'He does this every time, doesn't he?'
Mia turns the tap on and lowers her voice. The cloth keeps working the same corner of the island.
'I don't want to go. Isn't that stupid? Everything's packed and I don't want to go.' She looks at the doorway. 'If he says anything about me tonight, you know me, right?'
'We packed all day. Together. Didn't leave the flat once,' Julian says. At the same moment Mia says, 'I was lying down. I had a headache. I didn't see anything.' They both stop.
'You always make me clean up your mess.' 'I cleaned up yours.' A glass wobbles on the crate; Mia catches it. Both of them turn to me: 'Tell her she's remembering it wrong.' 'Tell him.'
A buzzing, from inside Julian's jacket. His hand goes flat over the pocket; the screen glows through the cloth.
'Work,' he says. 'Australia's awake.' He goes out to the balcony. Mia watches the jacket go. 'He has two phones now. For the move.'
I hold up my phone. 'Leo called me twice this afternoon. He said he was coming here early.'
Mia has stopped wiping. Her hands are flat on the counter. 'He's not late,' she says. A long pause. 'He's here. He's been here the whole time.'
'Mia. Stop,' Julian says, too quietly. Both of them look at me.
Julian pours for everyone. Nobody drinks.
Mia tells the story of the night Leo drove two hours at midnight to fetch her from a party. She laughs, and then she doesn't.
For a while nobody says anything. Somewhere below, a car door slams.
My phone buzzes on the crate. Nora: 'I'm downstairs. His car is here. His location says he's in your building.' Julian: 'Don't answer it.'
A knock at the door. All three of us look at it. Nobody moves. Another knock.
Nora leaves. The door closes behind her. Julian folds the tablecloth. Mia doesn't move.
Six in the morning. The movers lift the crate. 'Heavy one.'
